findings.title: Minute firing still waits for the entire unbounded pass
findings.description: `fire_unit_until` runs `mt-run minute` synchronously before it checks the journal for the trailing-complete marker. The wrapper’s `start_and_stream` waits until the service is inactive, so the cutover cannot reach its marker check or stop the unit until the full pass ends. This defeats the new bounded-firing behavior and can leave the cutover waiting through backfill until quota runs out. See `deploy/mt-run:127-129`.

findings.title: The limited sudoers rules do not authorize required cutover commands
findings.description: The root rule does not include the defined `MT_INSTALL` alias, so `install()` cannot run the installer under this policy. It also has no permission for the Python command used by `_repair()` to run `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py`. As a result, the cutover’s install and repair steps are rejected when relying on this limited ruleset. The relevant invocations are in `scripts/cutover_common.py:130` and `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:93`.

findings.title: The wildcard mt-run permission grants much broader root access than the cutover needs
findings.description: `MT_RUN` permits any arguments to the root-owned wrapper. For non-wrapper verbs, `deploy/mt-run` passes those arguments to the production `mt` CLI as root, allowing more than the minute and daily pass commands used by this cutover. Restrict the rule to the specific commands needed rather than granting the wrapper’s full CLI surface.

findings.title: A never-successful cagg refresh can crash verification instead of returning WAIT
findings.description: The query reads `last_successful_finish` without normalizing `-infinity`. The project’s cagg freshness code documents that TimescaleDB can return this value for a policy that has never completed a run, and that psycopg raises `DataError` when decoding it. In that state, `--verify` crashes before it can report a stale cagg as `[WAIT]`; normalize the value to `NULL` in the query.

findings.title: The changed acquisition path has no realistic load test
findings.description: The new per-chunk session-bounds lookup and session-based outcome judgment are covered by unit tests, but the load test in `test/load/test_921_minute_session_mass_nfr.py` exercises the health mass read, not the minute daemon’s provider/database path. The required load-test coverage for changed network/acquisition code should exercise a realistic daemon configuration and assert resource or latency bounds.
